clue.text: Adventurer's truism on vice? He's in fashion

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: a self-evident statement about vice is 'sin (is) bad'

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a tailor works in fashion, making clothes
taken as written, with the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A moral platitude about wickedness, and a man said to be in the fashion trade.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Adventurer's' stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay; 'fashion' reads as a trend but is the tailor's trade.
explanation.definitionFit: The seafaring hero of the Arabian Nights tales sails off on seven voyages of adventure.

clue.text: See 21
Saucy chap in a state between mounts

indicators.note: between tells us the state sits in the gap separating the two mountain words

parts.note: a ben is a Scottish mountain
a hill is a smaller mount
NY is the abbreviation for New York state

explanation.surface: A cheeky fellow found in some American state lying between mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: BENNY HILL was a British TV comedian famous for saucy, innuendo-laden sketches. 'mounts' gives both BEN and HILL.
explanation.definitionFit: The comedian's show was notorious for its cheeky, risqué humour, making him a byword for a saucy chap.

clue.text: Revolutionary army fight a hundred in friendly location, missing conclusion

parts.note: to vie is to compete or fight

indicators.note: in tells us the hundred goes inside the shortened location
missing conclusion means the final letter of the place name is dropped

parts.note: Tonga is known as the Friendly Islands
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A rebel force battles a hundred men in a welcoming place but never finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Tonga was named the Friendly Islands by Captain Cook; 'missing conclusion' cuts it to TONG, and 'in' puts C inside to make TCONG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Communist guerrilla force fought in South Vietnam during the Vietnam War, a revolutionary army.

clue.text: Instance of relief taking two minutes?

indicators.note: two tells us the same small word appears twice in a row

parts.note: minute in the sense of tiny means wee

explanation.surface: Someone takes a short two-minute break to relieve themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minutes' is read as the adjective minute (my-NEWT), tiny, not units of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's word for urinating, which is relieving oneself.

clue.text: Drug deeper in, unfortunately, having injected heroin

indicators.note: having injected tells us one piece is put inside the other
unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drug user goes deeper into addiction, sadly, after injecting heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges DEEPER IN, and 'having injected' puts H into that mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A stimulant drug used as a decongestant and once abused as an amphetamine substitute.

clue.text: See 17
Sweetheart having to feed baby, lovely thing for old song

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment
to suckle is to breastfeed an infant
a rose is a beautiful flower

explanation.surface: A lover feeds an infant, a lovely act, while an old tune plays.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1929 jazz standard by Fats Waller, now an old song.

clue.text: Hebrew puts one king back in place

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in tells us the reversed king goes inside the place

parts.note: a site is a location

indicators.note: back means the king's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's legendary king

explanation.surface: A Jewish man puts one monarch back where he belongs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the king's name into RAEL, which 'in' places after the first letter of the place word; 'puts' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israelite was a member of the ancient Hebrew people.

clue.text: Shot illegally taken in outskirts of Palermo

indicators.note: in tells us the stolen word sits inside the outside letters
outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters of the city

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A stolen shot taken on the edge of a Sicilian city.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is a photograph, as in a snapshot.

clue.text: Bend in front of bird, one tied up

indicators.note: in front of tells us the bending word comes first

parts.note: to bow is to bend at the waist
the knot is a wading bird

explanation.surface: Someone bows before a bird, one of them bound.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow knot is a decorative tie, so it is something that has been tied up.

clue.text: Riding feat by infant, really pronounced?

indicators.note: a small child often says W for R, so this is how the word comes out of a toddler
pronounced tells us we hear the word spoken rather than see it spelt

parts.note: a toddler says really as 'weally'

explanation.surface: A trick on a bike performed by a toddler, said with real emphasis.
explanation.walkthrough: A small child turns R into W, so 'really' comes out 'weally', which is said the same as the stunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclist's stunt of riding balanced on the back wheel alone.

clue.text: Those spotted keeping king happy losing heart, seeing saucy chap

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the king goes within

parts.note: dice are spotted cubes
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: losing heart means one middle letter is removed

parts.note: merry means happy

explanation.surface: Gamblers' dice hold a cheerful king who loses heart on seeing a cheeky fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: DICK EMERY was a British TV comedian known for saucy characters. 'losing heart' drops one central R from MERRY, giving MERY.
explanation.definitionFit: The comedian's catchphrase-laden, innuendo-filled characters made him a cheeky, saucy chap.

clue.text: Yellow eggs retrieved, left in canteen, not far off

indicators.note: in tells us the colour, eggs and left go inside the canteen

parts.note: a mess is a military dining hall
or is the heraldic name for gold or yellow

indicators.note: retrieved is read as brought back, so the eggs word is read in reverse

parts.note: roe is fish eggs

explanation.surface: Yellow eggs are brought back and left in the canteen, nearly there.
explanation.walkthrough: Heraldry calls yellow or gold 'or'. 'retrieved' turns the eggs into EOR, and 'in' puts the colour, eggs and left inside the canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means approximately, so roughly close to the mark.

clue.text: Use rating to work out mark

indicators.note: to work out suggests the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Use a grading system to work out a score.
explanation.definitionFit: A signature is a person's distinguishing mark written on a document.

clue.text: May author Stephen be his name?

definitions.text: May author Stephen be his name?

parts.note: may blossom is hawthorn, whose berry is the haw
Stephen King is the horror novelist

explanation.surface: Could another famous Stephen be named after hawthorn and a horror novelist?
explanation.walkthrough: May is the hawthorn tree, whose fruit is a haw. The whole clue points at the physicist Stephen Hawking.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmologist Stephen Hawking shares a first name with the novelist King, so the clue asks if his surname fits.

clue.text: Kelly, seeing sex appeal in the mirror, covered initially in one's make-up?

parts.note: Gene Kelly was the dancer and film star

indicators.note: a mirror shows things backwards, so the word is read reversed

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A film star sees his allure reflected in a mirror, first covered in makeup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the mirror' turns IT into TI. 'make-up' looks like cosmetics but means constitution.
explanation.definitionFit: Genetic traits are inherited ones, part of one's biological constitution.

clue.text: Camp tune with which naughty leader in concert band having a ball?

indicators.note: in tells us the leading letter sits inside the concert

parts.note: a gig is a live concert

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: a gang is a band of people
goolie is British slang for a testicle

explanation.surface: A scouting song in which a naughty bandleader at a concert is enjoying himself.
explanation.walkthrough: GING GANG GOOLIE is a nonsense song sung at Scout camps. 'leader' gives N from 'naughty', put 'in' GIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional nonsense song sung by Scouts around the campfire at camp.

clue.text: Attempted to gather everyone to be tested

indicators.note: to gather means to collect inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: tried means attempted
all means everyone

explanation.surface: An effort is made to collect everybody for examination.
explanation.definitionFit: To have trialled something is to have put it through a test.

clue.text: Used to support, help

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
a hand is help, as in lend a hand

explanation.surface: Something was used to support and help.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand goods have been owned and used before.

clue.text: Decent hospital dividing class

indicators.note: dividing means splitting the other word by sitting inside it

parts.note: a caste is a social class

explanation.surface: A respectable hospital splits up the social classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and modest, so decent in conduct.

clue.text: Slightly absurd greeting our leader, having broken vow after repeated inconsistency in leadership?

clue.text: See 3
See 13
Beef and carrots may be hot and bothered

parts.note: meat and vegetables cooked slowly together in a pot are in a casserole dish

explanation.surface: A cook notes that beef and carrots can end up flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the phrase describes stewed meat; idiomatically it means agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in a state of anxiety or agitation.

clue.text: Good novelist getting better?

parts.note: Eric Ambler was a British thriller writer

explanation.surface: A fine author improving, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like the comparative of good, but it is one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A better is a person who bets, a punter or gambler.

clue.text: Animal decapitating rat

indicators.note: decapitating means cutting off the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a rotter is a rat, a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A creature bites the head off a rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rat' is a cad, ROTTER, not the rodent; losing its head leaves the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A river-dwelling mammal of the weasel family, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Two seconds after we enrol, surprisingly free from proprietor

indicators.note: after means the two seconds come at the end
surprisingly suggests an unexpected order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
the second S for the second second

explanation.surface: Two seconds after we sign up, unexpectedly nobody owns us.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ownerless has no owner, so it is without any proprietor.
